newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks crawl higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks crawl higher at open.

text.p: The Australian share market crawled higher at the open on Monday with weak signals from overseas markets failing to inspire much commitment from traders.
From opening, the All Ordinaries index added 3.7 points to 2,427.4.

Industrials had the best run in early trade, firming after a rally in U.S. bonds, while miners were mixed with mild losses in bellwether BHP and a softer gold sector just outweighing modest gains in other resource leaders.
"It is about what we expected," said dealer Brett O'Donovan of Brisbane-based broker Lance Jones.
"We thought it would be fairly thin and quiet with a ten point range and it's been a little more on the positive side," he added, pointing to the mixed bag of performances so far.

"Volumes aren't tremendous. There is a bit of excitement in News Corp ahead of its results and a bit of selling in BHP that is a flow on from options expiry late last week, and that is continuing today, but it is all fairly mild."

Biota impressed early, its shares up 9.7 percent to A$3.85 (US$2.94) after favourable press coverage of its influenza drug. Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to four, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
